conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.question: In John 1:8, John the Baptist is presented as the light that came into the world.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.learningObjective: Observe that John the Baptist points to the light but is not the light.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.feedbackCorrect: The text says the opposite: "Não era ele a luz". John came to bear witness to the light.

feedbackWrong.true: Reread John 1:8: John was not the light; he came to bear witness to the light.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-01.hint: Look at the beginning of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.question: In John 1:1, tap who was with God in the beginning.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.learningObjective: Identify the Word as the one who was with God in the beginning.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.feedbackCorrect: The Word was already with God in the beginning; John uses this name for Jesus.

feedbackWrong.b: "Era" is the verb of the sentence; tap who was with God.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-02.hint: Look for the name that repeats three times in the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-03.question: According to John 1:12, what do those who welcome the Word receive?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-03.learningObjective: Observe what John promises to those who receive the Word.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-03.feedbackCorrect: Whoever receives the Word and believes in his name gains the right to become a child of God.

feedbackWrong.a: Verse 13 says these children are not born of blood, but of God.
feedbackWrong.b: The light here is Jesus; what is received is becoming a child of God.
feedbackWrong.d: The text does not speak of becoming a prophet; it speaks of becoming a child of God.

options.a: A guaranteed place among the people of Israel
options.b: The ability to see the light with their eyes
options.c: The right to become children of God
options.d: The right to be prophets like John

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-04.question: Put John 1:14 together in the order of the text.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-04.feedbackCorrect: That is the verse's order: the Word comes to live among us, full of grace, and his glory is seen.

feedbackWrong.default: Start with the Word becoming flesh; the glory seen comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-04.hint: The verse begins with the Word.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.question: In John 1:5, where does the light shine?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the image of the light shining in the dark.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.feedbackCorrect: The light shines right in the dark, and the darkness cannot put it out.

feedbackWrong.a: Waters recall Genesis 1, but here the light shines in the dark.
feedbackWrong.b: The light does not stay far off, up high; it shines where it is dark.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-05.hint: Think of the opposite of light.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.question: What does John 1:14 say that connects to this context?
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.learningObjective: Connect John 1:14 to the human life of Jesus.
conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.feedbackCorrect: "Se fez carne": the Word, who was God, came to live as a human being among us.

feedbackWrong.a: The text says the opposite: he lived among us.
feedbackWrong.c: John says "se fez carne": not an appearance, but a truly human life.

conhecer-a-deus-sem-entrada-deus-05-06.hint: See what the Word became and where he lived.

options.a: The Word stayed far away, in heaven
options.b: The Word became a human being
options.c: The Word appeared only as a vision

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.question: In John 1:10, the world was made through the Word, and even so it did not know him.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.learningObjective: Understand the contrast between the Creator and the world that did not know him.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.feedbackCorrect: "No entanto" marks the contrast: the world came from him, yet did not recognize him.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread John 1:10: the world was made through him; yet the world did not know him.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-01.hint: Notice the expression that links the two parts of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.question: In John 1:12, tap the word that marks the turn after the rejection in the previous verse.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.learningObjective: Recognize the marker of contrast between rejection and welcome.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.feedbackCorrect: "Mas" turns the page: his own did not receive him, but whoever does becomes a child of God.

feedbackWrong.a: "Deu-lhes" shows the gift received, not the turn itself.
feedbackWrong.b: "Todos" tells the reach; the turn comes before, in the first word.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-02.hint: Look for a short word at the start of the verse.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-03.question: In John 1:7–8, how does John the Baptist relate to the light?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-03.learningObjective: Relate John the Baptist's mission to the light.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-03.feedbackCorrect: John is a witness: he points to the light so that everyone may come to believe.

feedbackWrong.b: There is no rivalry: he came to bear witness about the light.
feedbackWrong.c: John 1:8 says: "Não era ele a luz".
feedbackWrong.d: The purpose is wide: "a fim de que todos viessem a crer".

options.a: He points to the light, so that others may believe
options.b: He competes with the light for the people's faith
options.c: He is the light, sent before the Word
options.d: He keeps the light only for his own disciples

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-04.question: In what order does John present the Word in John 1:1–14?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-04.learningObjective: Understand the movement of John's prologue.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-04.feedbackCorrect: First who he is, then what he did in creation, and then his coming to live among us.

feedbackWrong.default: John starts in the beginning, moves through creation, and arrives at the Word made flesh.

options.a: The eternal Word, with God and God
options.b: All things were made through him
options.c: The Word comes to live among us

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.question: In John 1:11, what did his own fail to do with the Word?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the action that separates rejection from welcome.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.feedbackCorrect: He came to his own, and they did not receive him: the rejection sets up the turn in verse 12.

feedbackWrong.a: "Conheceu" appears in John 1:10, about the world; here the verb is different.
feedbackWrong.c: The text does not speak of following; it speaks of welcoming the one who came.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-05.hint: Verse 12 repeats the same verb, now in the positive.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.question: What links John 1:1 to Genesis 1:1?
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.learningObjective: Relate the beginning of John to the beginning of Genesis.
conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.feedbackCorrect: John begins like Genesis to show that the Word was already there when everything began.

feedbackWrong.a: In the beginning, the Word already was; he was not created.
feedbackWrong.c: John speaks of the same creation; all things were made through the Word.

conhecer-a-deus-cam-entrada-deus-05-06.hint: Compare the first words of the two verses.

options.a: The Word created in the beginning
options.c: Two different creations of the world

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.question: John 1:1–2 shows the Word already with God in the beginning, not as something God created later.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.learningObjective: Distinguish the eternal Word from a creature.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.feedbackCorrect: The Word already was in the beginning, was with God and was God; all things were made through him.

feedbackWrong.false: Reread: "No princípio, era o Verbo". He does not appear later; he was already beside God.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-01.hint: See where the Word was in the beginning.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.question: In John 1:5, tap the phrase that shows the light still stands in the face of evil.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.learningObjective: Support from the text that the light is not overcome.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.feedbackCorrect: Darkness is real, but it has not overcome the light: the last word belongs to the light.

feedbackWrong.a: "Nas trevas" shows where it shines, not how the clash ends.
feedbackWrong.b: "A luz" tells who shines; what shows it holds firm comes at the end.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-02.hint: Look at what the darkness could not do.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.question: What reading does John 1:14 support about how God makes himself known?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.learningObjective: Choose the reading the text supports about God revealing himself in Jesus.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.feedbackCorrect: The Word lived among us, and his glory was seen: in Jesus, God lets himself be known.

feedbackWrong.b: John says "vimos a sua glória": God let himself be seen up close.
feedbackWrong.c: "Se fez carne" affirms real humanity, not an appearance.
feedbackWrong.d: In the beginning, the Word already was, and was God (John 1:1).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-03.hint: Compare each option with "habitou entre nós" and "vimos".

options.a: God shows himself in Jesus, who lived among us
options.b: God remains distant, and no one sees his glory
options.c: Jesus only seemed human, like an apparition
options.d: The Word was the first thing God created

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.question: Which sequence shows the thread of God living with his people that runs through John 1:14?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.learningObjective: See John 1:14 within the thread of God coming to live with his people.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.feedbackCorrect: From the tent in the desert to Jesus among us, and at last God living with his people.

feedbackWrong.default: Follow the story: the desert (Ex 40:34), Jesus (John 1:14), and the end (Rev 21:3).

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-04.hint: Follow the order of the Bible: Exodus, the Gospels, Revelation.

options.a: The glory of the Lord fills the tent in the desert
options.b: The Word dwells among us and we see his glory
options.c: God comes to live with his people forever

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.question: In John 1:14, what did the Word do among us after becoming flesh?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.learningObjective: Remember the term that shows God coming to live close by.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.feedbackCorrect: To dwell is to live alongside, like pitching a tent among the people: God truly near.

feedbackWrong.a: It was not a quick visit; the text speaks of living among the people.
feedbackWrong.c: He also spoke, but the verse says more: he lived among us.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-05.hint: The verb is about living somewhere, not visiting.

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.question: What links John 1:3 to Hebrews 1:1–2?
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.learningObjective: Connect the creating Word in John to the Son in Hebrews.
conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.feedbackCorrect: Both texts say the same thing: it was through the Son that God made all things.

feedbackWrong.a: The texts do not place the Son among the things made; all things were made through him.
feedbackWrong.c: The Son was already at work in creation: "through whom he also made the universe".

conhecer-a-deus-pro-entrada-deus-05-06.hint: See through whom things were made in both texts.

options.b: All things were made by the Son

estudo:entrada-deus-05.context: John opens his Gospel with the same words as Genesis: "No princípio". He calls Jesus the Word, that is, the Word of God. Before telling what Jesus did, John says who he is and where he comes from.
estudo:entrada-deus-05.focusQuestion: Looking at Jesus, what do you learn about what God is like?
estudo:entrada-deus-05.keywordGloss: The Word of God; John uses this name for Jesus, who shows God in person.
facts: The Word was with God and was God.
All things were made through the Word.
The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
John the Baptist came to bear witness to the light, but he was not the light.
Whoever receives the Word gains the right to become a child of God.
The Word became flesh and lived among us.
